title: Spilcaféen
concept: In this first-semester project, I redesigned SpilCaféen's game catalog to make it more intuitive and user-friendly. While built upon an initial group assignment, this individual exam project allowed me to independently iterate on and elevate the final solution.
We had to independently identify the target audience and analyze their behavior using user studies and observations.
The design of the page is inspired by Spilcaféen's original website

contributions.heading: Idea & Structure
contributions.text: Before branching into an individual exam project, our team mapped out a flowchart for the overview page and used Object-Oriented UX (OOUX) principles to structure the content precisely. This foundational mapping allowed us to explore targeted design concepts for each individual element.

contributions.heading: Inspiration
contributions.text: When approaching the design phase, I found inspiration from platforms I frequently use myself. I drew inspiration from multi-location barber websites and Pricerunner's clean, structured layout for filter menus and product cards, remixing these elements into my final design where it fit.

contributions.heading: Variation from design
contributions.text: Translating the design into code as a first-semester student taught me how to balance ambition with practical execution. I realized that code sometimes requires pragmatic compromises, and that implementation can occasionally spark improvements that weren't in the original prototype. While this particular project reflects where I was at that stage of my education, it serves as a great benchmark for how much my technical skills have evolved since then.

reflections: Created during my first semester when my JavaScript experience was still limited, this project was a breakthrough for my CSS and HTML structuring, making layout spacing much easier to manage. It also involved adapting existing codebase elements; while I didn't fully grasp how the logic worked at the time, modifying and breaking down that code taught me a lot about practical implementation.
buttonSummary: A website designed to provide a better overview of board games.

title: Uniquely Her
concept: In this second-semester project, we created a retail web shop for women. 'Uniquely Her' is an all-in-one destination offering fitness clothes in multiple colors and fits to suit all women—not just slim ones.

We worked with a self-selected target audience to define the scope of the web shop. However, we dove deeper using research and performed segmentation to ensure we knew exactly who we were designing for.
The design was approached through a feminist lens, making it unmistakably clear that it was created for women.

contributions.heading: Research
contributions.text: Through research into the problem space, we explored major retail web shops and compared their women's and men's fitness clothes selections. We also analysed how they made their UX/UI design wich gave us deeper insight into the conventions used by leading platforms.

contributions.heading: Target group
contributions.text: Desk research revealed that while women have more fitness wear options overall, major retailers rely exclusively on athletic models—leaving the plus-size community underrepresented. To bridge this gap, 'Uniquely Her' prioritizes inclusive sizing and comfort for all body types, balancing athletic and plus-size clothes.

contributions.heading: Identety, design & vibe
contributions.text: To define our brand identity, we established five core values: body-positive, motivating, fresh, relatable, and feminine. This resulted in a vibrant, feminine design featuring a playful, approachable tone—which is especially reflected in our custom title font and assets.

reflections: I learned how filter menus actually function under the hood. Beyond that, I realized how rewarding it is to analyze existing solutions, add your own unique twist, and build something custom. Finally, I gained valuable experience in diving headfirst into a subject I knew nothing about. I am a man after all.
buttonSummary: A webshop featuring fitness clothing to woman of all shapes and sizes.

title: Mer' end Toast
concept: For this second-semester project, we developed an app that brings together recipe searching, item and recipe pricing, and a shopping list into a single app.

The target audience was defined based on people looking to save money on food. Students were an obvious choice, and the name “Mer' end Toast” was selected because every young person i Denmark knows toast and knows it is an inexpensive snack, but this app is more than just toast.
Design and content were determined through detailed research involving user studies and competitor conventions.

contributions.heading: Research of conventions
contributions.text: Through a thorough competitor analysis of 10 similar platforms during the discover phase, we identified market standards and pinpointed areas where we could stand out.

contributions.heading: Functions
contributions.text: Our insights showed that Mer' end Toast would create the greatest value by integrating into as many parts of the users' cooking workflow as possible. Therefore, we prioritized two core features: price comparison between recipes with updates based on weekly promotional flyers, and a shopping list.

contributions.heading: Technical challenge
contributions.text: The most technical challenge was then building a well-structured database of recipes containing ingredients with units. Each ingredient would also need to include pricing and nutritional values.

reflections: I learned how to use CRUD and Supabase even better and now have a great reference for future projects. In addition, I gained more experience with Jitter and Lottie animations.
buttonSummary: A recipe app that combines recipes, pricing, and shopping lists into one single app.

title: mellemrum
concept: For this 3rd-semester project, I further developed and optimized Mellemrum—a fictional client focused on making it easy and straightforward to discover local events and workshops in Aarhus.
From there, our task was to analyze the website and identify the issues and areas for improvement that needed to be addressed.

contributions.heading: Testing
contributions.text: Before making any changes to the website, I first walked through the existing user experience. I tested the core user flow from finding an event and viewing its details, to signing up and checking existing registrations. After identifying the main surface-level UX issues on [mellemrum](https://cederdorff.com/mellemrum/), I dived into the codebase to pinpoint technical improvements like missing loading states or micro interactions. I compiled everything into an [audit](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1u0zaH6SHVuLxZm12Ho-dUiabJRMWlwzboKWH-qSA6kU/edit?usp=sharing) documenting the identified problems and proposed solutions.

contributions.heading: Examination
contributions.text: My [Audit](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1u0zaH6SHVuLxZm12Ho-dUiabJRMWlwzboKWH-qSA6kU/edit?usp=sharing) details the full scope of issues and areas for improvement. I organized my findings under descriptive headings and prioritized each task based on severity. For example, navigating to an event was restricted to clicking a 'Read more' button. Since standard web conventions allow users to click directly on the image, I updated the code accordingly. For the loading state to work, I made a try-catch logic that also helped error prevention. For each observation, I supported the issue with UX theory and applied established industry standards to design an optimal solution.

contributions.heading: Results
contributions.text: I managed to fix virtually all the issues I identified, but the project wasn't based solely on self-assessment. My [Audit](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1u0zaH6SHVuLxZm12Ho-dUiabJRMWlwzboKWH-qSA6kU/edit?usp=sharing) included a dedicated section outlining how each solution would be tested to verify if the issue was resolved. Based on my user testing and lighthouse, I ensured that my version of [mellemrum](https://jeppekorsgaard.com/case-1-mellemrum/) performs better in terms of usability and accessibility. Additionally, the Supabase data structure was optimized into a cleaner format, making it much easier to maintain and scale in the long run.

contributions.heading: Value & Potential
contributions.text: The core value delivered in this project lies in enhancing the overall user experience by applying established web conventions from comparable platforms. This directly benefits primary users looking to discover and sign up for events by reducing friction and cognitive load throughout the user journey. Secondarily, it creates business value for Mellemrum, as a more intuitive and seamless platform minimizes drop-off rates and increases successful event registrations.

reflections: This project provided valuable insights into code optimization and UX-driven problem-solving. Working with a structured audit proved highly effective, pushing me to combine UX theory with solutions. I wanted to make a standard log in flow, but ended up implementing a simpler alternative instead. The focus on code rather than visual design made me focus strictly on usability by preventing user frustration. As a next step, developing a dedicated Organizer View would be the ideal addition. Leveraging the existing sign-up data structure, this would complete the ecosystem by giving event creators a seamless overview.
buttonSummary: Uptimizing a local event platform in code.

title: vuuh
concept: For this 3rd-semester project, the goal was to redesign the onboarding experience for Vuuh—a Shopify app that helps retailers effortlessly discover and display products from distributors.
The main scope was to help non-technical users quickly understand the platform's value, encouraging them to convert into paying customers and integrate Vuuh into their own webshops.

The process began with diagnosing friction points in the existing onboarding experience, followed by a full redesign to improve user flow. Finally, we audited and qualified the solution's accessibility to ensure an inclusive platform for a broader user base.

contributions.heading: Testing
contributions.text: We began with a presentation of Vuuh's value proposition and Shopify app capabilities, followed by analyzing their existing user flows and visuals. To evaluate the interface, we conducted a heuristic evaluation, listing each finding to specific design principles, user friction points, and solution proposals. To maintain a sharp scope, we narrowed our focus to the 'Connect to Shopify' flow and performed a cognitive walkthrough. By breaking down every step in the process, we evaluated whether non-technical users could easily discover actions, understand their intent, execute them correctly, and receive clear feedback on their progress.

contributions.heading: Examination
contributions.text: We synthesized our findings to highlight the core issues: an overcomplicated 'Connect to Shopify' flow, dense Information Architecture (IA), a lack of system feedback, ambiguous terminology, and insufficient guidance for first-time users. Through this synthesis, we identified a recurring pattern: a critical lack of clarity and explanation especially for the targeted user throughout the experience. This provided us with actionable insights that opened up the design space without locking us into a single rigid solution.

contributions.heading: Results
contributions.text: Once we defined our specific objectives, we began the redesign and documented it all in a [UX Audit sumary](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1tDJplhxqCv8i2DzmckC-2Ac5gvmVL7HM/view?usp=sharing). Since our target audience required clearer guidance and immediate feedback, we introduced an interactive tutorial providing a preview of the app. Additionally, we implemented a wizard that tracks progress as users complete the necessary integration steps, with a primary focus on the 'Connect to Shopify' flow. Each page now features an explanatory banner detailing the page's purpose and implementation steps. To reassure users after actions are taken, success messages provide immediate confirmation and smoothly guide them back to the dashboard and wizard.

contributions.heading: Value & Potential
contributions.text: This redesign transforms a high-friction onboarding flow into an intuitive, guided experience for non-technical users. By streamlining the Information Architecture and introducing features like a progress-tracking wizard, introductory tutorial, and contextual banners, the solution minimizes user drop-off and eases the 'Connect to Shopify' process. As outlined in the UX Audit summary, this delivers clear business value for Vuuh by driving conversions and improving overall accessibility.

reflections: This project provided valuable insights into making a structure for uptimizing user flows by just testing it on myself, but still having a strong basis from heuritic theory. An example is 'help and documentation': a manual shouldn't be necessary and 'visibility of system': the user should know what's going on. Thats just naming a few, but im sure there could be more changes to make, but we chose to focus on a specific flow. Next steps could include implementing interactive dashboard tooltips or analytics tracking to monitor drop-offs and friction points.
buttonSummary: Uptimizing a shopify app about product data.
